From 34080db3e70ddf94c38512ad2331e3c3afca6cc1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 12:24:48 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] net/rds: fix NULL deref in rds_ib_send_cqe_handler() on
 masked atomic completion

rds_ib_xmit_atomic() always programs a masked atomic opcode
(IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP or IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD)
for every RDS atomic cmsg.  But the completion-side switch in
rds_ib_send_unmap_op() only handles the non-masked opcodes, so a masked
atomic completion falls through to default and returns rm == NULL while
send->s_op is left set.  rds_ib_send_cqe_handler() then dereferences the
NULL rm via rm->m_final_op, oopsing in softirq context.  An unprivileged
AF_RDS sendmsg() of an atomic cmsg over an active RDS/IB connection
triggers it; on hardware that natively accepts masked atomics (mlx4,
mlx5) no extra setup is needed.

  RDS/IB: rds_ib_send_unmap_op: unexpected opcode 0xd in WR!
  Oops: general protection fault [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000190-0x0000000000000197]
  RIP: rds_ib_send_cqe_handler+0x25c/0xb10 (net/rds/ib_send.c:282)
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   rds_ib_send_cqe_handler (net/rds/ib_send.c:282)
   poll_scq (net/rds/ib_cm.c:274)
   rds_ib_tasklet_fn_send (net/rds/ib_cm.c:294)
   tasklet_action_common (kernel/softirq.c:943)
   handle_softirqs (kernel/softirq.c:573)
   run_ksoftirqd (kernel/softirq.c:479)
   </IRQ>
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

Handle the masked atomic opcodes in the same case as the non-masked
ones: they map to the same struct rds_message.atomic union member, so
the existing container_of()/rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic() body is correct
for them.

Fixes: 20c72bd5f5f9 ("RDS: Implement masked atomic operations")
Reported-by: Xiang Mei <xmei5@asu.edu>
Signed-off-by: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Allison Henderson <achender@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260606192447.1179255-2-bestswngs@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/rds/ib_send.c b/net/rds/ib_send.c
index fcd04c29f543..d6be95542119 100644
--- a/net/rds/ib_send.c
+++ b/net/rds/ib_send.c
@@ -170,6 +170,8 @@ static struct rds_message *rds_ib_send_unmap_op(struct rds_ib_connection *ic,
 		break;
 	case IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD:
 	case IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP:
+	case IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD:
+	case IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP:
 		if (send->s_op) {
 			rm = container_of(send->s_op, struct rds_message, atomic);
 			rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic(ic, send->s_op, wc_status);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications per File

- **net/rds/ib_send.c**  
  Added two new case labels `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP` to the existing `switch` statement inside `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()`. These cases are placed alongside the already-handled non-masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`). The code body for these cases (mapping to `rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic()`) remains unchanged.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The single change in `rds/ib_send.c` directly addresses the root cause of the NULL pointer dereference. Previously, the completion handler `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` called `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()`, which only recognized non-masked atomic opcodes. When a masked atomic completion occurred (common on mlx4/mlx5 hardware), the switch defaulted, leaving `send->s_op` still set but returning `rm = NULL`. This caused a NULL dereference when accessing `rm->m_final_op`. By adding the masked atomic opcodes to the same case block, the function now correctly retrieves the associated `rds_message` via `container_of()` and unmaps the atomic operation, preventing the NULL dereference and the subsequent kernel panic. The two added lines are logically coupled: both masked atomic variants map to the same `struct rds_message.atomic` union member, so the same handling applies to both.

Here is the root cause:
The function `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` in `net/rds/ib_send.c` handles completion of work requests. It only includes case labels for non-masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`). However, `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()` programs masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD`) for every RDS atomic cmsg. When a masked atomic completion occurs, the switch statement falls through to the default case, which does not set `rm` (returns NULL) but leaves `send->s_op` set. The caller `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` then dereferences the NULL `rm` via `rm->m_final_op`, causing a NULL pointer dereference and kernel panic.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static struct rds_message *rds_ib_send_unmap_op(struct rds_ib_connection *ic,
 						struct rds_ib_send_work *send,
 						int wc_status)
 {
 	struct rds_message *rm = NULL;
 
 	/* In the error case, wc.opcode sometimes contains garbage */
 	switch (send->s_wr.opcode) {
 	case IB_WR_SEND:
 		if (send->s_op) {
 			rm = container_of(send->s_op, struct rds_message, data);
 			rds_ib_send_unmap_data(ic, send->s_op, wc_status);
 		}
 		break;
 	case IB_WR_RDMA_WRITE:
 	case IB_WR_RDMA_READ:
 		if (send->s_op) {
 			rm = container_of(send->s_op, struct rds_message, rdma);
 			rds_ib_send_unmap_rdma(ic, send->s_op, wc_status);
 		}
 		break;
 	case IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD:
 	case IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP:
+	case IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD:
+	case IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP:
 		if (send->s_op) {
 			rm = container_of(send->s_op, struct rds_message, atomic);
 			rds_ib_send_unmap_atomic(ic, send->s_op, wc_status);
 		}
 		break;
 	default:
 		printk_ratelimited(KERN_NOTICE
 			       "RDS/IB: %s: unexpected opcode 0x%x in WR!\n",
 			       __func__, send->s_wr.opcode);
 		break;
 	}
 
 	send->s_wr.opcode = 0xdead;
 
 	return rm;
 }
